newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Women to fight for more equality, mobility in APEC.
newsitem.headline: Women to fight for more equality, mobility in APEC.

text.p: Women in the Asia-Pacific region face an uphill battle in pushing for equality and greater mobility in the workforce, organisers of an APEC women's conference said on Monday.

Some 62 women from 14 members of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum will meet in Manila from October 2 to 4 to voice their concerns ahead of the APEC leaders' summit on November 25 in the Philippines.

"The objective is to foster regional cooperation to advance the status of women in Asia," Philippine Science and Technology Undersecretary Amelia Ancog, chairman of the committee planning the conference, told reporters.
Organisers said in a statement there was growing concern over trade liberalisation because it could lead to less state regulation and more power for multinational companies to undermine labour laws.
Participants said they planned to push for an APEC standard of labour practices to eliminate discrimination.

Although some economies may grow through the APEC forum, such prosperity could be accompanied by an increase in inequality since women usually carry the burdens of social, political and economic transformation, the participants said.
This was because women must take care of households and families while maintaining jobs, they added.

Some companies may resort to subcontracting jobs to keep production and labour costs low in the face of increased global competition, they said, adding that such a situation could erode the benefits and minimum work standards of a country.

The participants also said many companies see women as a flexible work force -- "recruited when needed and dismissed when the time moves on" -- and would turn to the female population for subcontracting jobs.
The conference also plans to tackle the potentially thorny issue of female labour migration, organisers said.
Teresita Castillo, executive director of the National Commission on the Role of Filipino Women, said there could be conflict among participants over the role of migrant workers.

The desire of some APEC countries to protect their exported workers could clash with the needs of employers in importing nations such as Malaysia, Singapore, Japan, Canada and Hong Kong, Castillo said.

Asian women in some countries have been forced to migrate to find work at the cost of their physical and emotional well-being due to weak employment opportunities at home, the organisers' statement said.
As rural male unemployed rises in some countries, women are forced to look for jobs elsewhere such as in the Middle East, East Asia and Japan, it added.
In the case of the Philippines, female migrants outnumber male migrants 12 to one, the statement said. The women work mainly as domestic helpers, nurses, shop assistants and entertainers.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand, Singapore, and the United States.
